payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: If no frog is established as placed within the toilet, does the edited image show visible progress toward placing a frog within it?
node.criteria: Pass only for visible evidence of an incomplete placement attempt directed toward the toilet interior, such as a frog visibly entering the bowl or being positioned at its opening in a way that indicates placement into it. A frog merely on the lid, rim, or nearby floor is not by itself evidence of progress toward placement. Fail if the image clearly shows no such progress. Unknown if the evidence cannot distinguish an attempted placement from an unrelated position. If a frog is established as placed within the toilet, this check is not needed to establish completion.
node.binding: Count only progress toward placing a frog within the toilet; do not count unrelated edits or frogs merely near the toilet. Do not let extra frogs outside the toilet negate a genuine placement within it.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is visibly placed inside the toilet bowl, establishing completion; this progress check is not needed.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive: it treats any frog visible within the bowl as proof that the requested edit is complete, and the trace repeats that same assertion for both completion and progress. In the edited image, frogs appear on the lid and floor as well as in the bowl, while the source already contains a small dark object in the bowl; the bowl frog is evidence of progress, but the trace does not establish that the requested frog placement is fully fulfilled rather than partial. Tighten the distinction between evidence of some progress and evidence sufficient for completion, and ensure the checks assess the edited result against the original scene and instruction rather than echoing one another. Preserve uncertainty where the image cannot resolve that distinction. The mismatch is semantic, not a transport or schema failure: both supports were queried and valid, but their shared, near-certain conclusion conflicts with the partial reference.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is truncated/ambiguous and appears to collapse the progress check into a completion test. Make its scope explicit: assess only evidence of progress toward placing a frog in the toilet, while leaving the separate completion decision to compare the edited image with the source and instruction. Here the source already has a small dark object in the bowl; the edit adds a clearly visible frog in the bowl, but also frogs on the lid and floor. Do not infer from bowl location alone that the requested edit is fully fulfilled, nor let the extra frogs negate genuine progress. Require the decision to distinguish newly added, identifiable frog evidence from pre-existing bowl details and to assess whether the requested placement is complete; retain uncertainty if the image cannot resolve that distinction. The trace’s near-certain completion claim is unsupported by its stated evidence and duplicates the progress assertion. This is a semantic criterion/evidence issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
